answer: Charge a non-transferable admission bond and bind it to one work channel whose transcripts are similarity-hashed each epoch. A second channel from the same hardware, key lineage, or near-duplicate text merges both records and slashes the stake. A basalt plinth supports only one timber hall; a second orchard planted on the same ledge shares roots, so the ledger treats the cluster as one organism. Buying a crowd then costs more than honest labor, because clones inherit one bond and one reputation, not many.
